## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Maṇḍūkadevaputtavimānavatthu* (Vv 51) is a verse narrative in the *Vimānavatthu* collection of the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. In this text, a celestial being (*deva*) relates his former existence as an animal—specifically a frog—and recounts how he attained his divine rebirth and powers after hearing the Buddha or Dharma [SuttaCentral; Hsu 2018]. SuttaCentral records five translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral].
Although SuttaCentral lists no independent parallel texts in other canonical collections [SuttaCentral], DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse with five other works, comprising 18 matching segments [DharmaNexus]. These matches include citations in Buddhaghosa’s *Visuddhimagga* (Paṭhamo bhāgo) as well as several canonical commentaries: the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Dukanipāta-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Modern scholarship similarly notes that this tale of the frog hearing the Dharma and gaining miraculous rebirth is framed through commentary and circulated widely across Theravāda literature and its East Asian transmission via texts such as the *Shanjianlü* [Hsu 2018].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0506a) (§2.1–4.4 ↔ §2341–2351_0); Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk Vin01a) (§0.4–2.4 ↔ §581_10–585); Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0201a) (§0.4–1.4 ↔ §662–663); Aṅguttaranikāye Dukanipāta-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0402a) (§0.4–1.4 ↔ §53–54); Visuddhimaggo (Paṭhamo bhāgo) (Anya E0101n) (§0.4–2.4 ↔ §1276_6–1280)
